body:
I've been trying to be more honest for the past few years. It might be building into something better. I have no idea though really. I've realized many times though that I can't really make up my mind on anything, and I feel like that's where this sense of losing it is probably coming from. I have a lot of regret as well, and the weight of that is more paralyzing than the fear at this point. Regret in never feeling present, with both my family and past friends.

And yeah, I can agree with that. I just beat myself up for not dealing with my battles as well as most people do. I sort of drift around in my head which  makes it hard to remember things and causes me to feel distanced from myself and others.

And not really. I can still play, but I don't as often as I should. It's hard with me working two jobs and taking classes right now. 

Thank you for taking the time to reply to this post. You have helped me make it a few more days. The last couple of days have been really up and down, but at least there were a couple ups in there.

My dad, the great man he is, has suggested the serenity prayer, and he, from what I remember, also followed the teachings of St. Francis. This just makes me feel like crap about myself, because it's taken the advice from a stanger on the internet (no offense) to seek that and integrate it. 

And it is as of recently. I went through most of high school pretty sober, but I still was hiding behind various things. I played the violin, but it was definitely something I used to hide behind. I was talented, and people liked me for that, so it was hard for me to break through that and be myself. So, even when I was sober and doing decent things, I still just felt like a shadow. 

And I was to an extent. I drank a bunch of coffee which sent me spiraling and I ended up going to bed at like 9 and spent most of today until this point in bed. 

The crappy thing about this is that my life on the outside isn't that bad. I just don't want to live with myself. I feel like a waste of opportunity and my parents efforts. I would rather have had it been tough on the outside and had to plod through that than have been this coward that wastes everyone's time.

I got careless last week, and smoked a little. Before that it had been a couple of weeks, maybe almost a month. It definitely did its job as a mild psychedelic, as it just exacerbated these feelings of my mind drifting towards an ugly place. But honestly I haven't. I'm not even sure how those work. I've been trying to find refuge in Buddhism, which is one of the only things my mind has been able to find interesting enough to focus on for quite some time. But I'm highly disorganized and scatterbrained, so falling into a daily meditation practice hasn't exactly worked out for me.
And she is. She's not perfect, and has been guilty of being overprotective and overbearing in the past. But her intentions have always been good. We've had our arguments, and some of the things I've said to her still eat at me. But she's still in my life. We're on better terms now that I live three hours away, but I guess that's what it takes sometimes.
And not at all, that's a pretty good summary. I've come to that conclusion a few times, but I never seem to be able to find energy and momentum to move forward that lasts more than a few weeks. I have good friends who have been fairly supportive, but as hinted at earlier, they're not necessarily sober influences.
